summary: Persistent silent tail and duplicated prefix tokens after short SSE disconnect when batched behind customer edge-proxy
description:
Issue summary:
BrightTutor reports intermittent partial responses where the stream completes tokens but there is no terminal event (no 'event: done' / no explicit end marker). Customers see repeated prefix tokens on manual client reconnect and in some cases a silent tail: the stream hangs without producing final punctuation or final metadata.

Impact:
- Customer-facing tutoring sessions occasionally end with partial answer text and no finalization marker.
- Manual reconnects (client-initiated SSE resume) sometimes replay the last 4-10 tokens at the start of the resumed stream (duplicate prefix) instead of continuing.
- Downstream UX shows duplicate phrases and missing final sentence  (~5-10% of long streaming requests during peak hours).

Environment:
- BrightTutor is on a Dedicated plan with private ingress through their edge proxy (Nginx with HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 upstream) forwarding to Redwood's API Gateway in us-east-1.
- Request path: Browser -> BrightTutor edge (HTTP/2) -> BrightTutor reverse-proxy (translates to HTTP/1.1) -> Redwood API Gateway -> Serving runtime (batched inference).
- Observed on redwood-v1-small and gptj-13b-quantized.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Start a chat generation request from their web client with streaming SSE and a long response (expected ~250-400 tokens).
2. During token emission, a short network blip (100-400ms) occurs between the browser and BrightTutor edge (simulated by their QA using tc/netem).
3. Client reconnects and resumes the SSE stream using the session_id and last_offset.
4. On resume, the client sometimes receives the last ~4-10 tokens again at the head of the resumed stream and never receives the final 'done' event; stream stays open for ~30s then client times out.

Observed logs & traces:
- API Gateway access logs show a normal initial POST then a second resume GET for the same session_id shortly after. Upstream latency spikes to 250-350ms during the blip.
- Serving runtime trace for one sample shows a batched inference group with prefetch buffer enabled; the batch commit for that request shows a partial flush followed by an incomplete end_of_stream event for the SSE session.
- Edge proxy (customer) logs show HTTP/2 connection reusing/multiplexing behavior and occasional stream resets (RST_STREAM) during blips.

Reproducibility:
- Customer reproduces locally under load when simulating short TLS/HTTP/2 resets at the edge. Not 100% deterministic, 1-8% of runs show the duplication + silent tail. More likely when multiple requests share the same batch window (continuous batching enabled).

Immediate mitigation (customer):
- Disable client-side automatic SSE resume (forces full retry) — reduces duplicate prefix but increases token cost.
- Temporarily lower batching window on BrightTutor side (shorten time-window that groups requests) which reduced occurrence in their tests.

Requested outcome:
- Root cause analysis and a permanent fix or recommended configuration to avoid duplicate prefixes and ensure terminal event reliably delivered after short disconnects and resume behind HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 proxies.
comments: Support - Asha Patel (2026-03-10): Logged initial report from BrightTutor. Customer provided packet captures, API Gateway traces, and their edge Nginx config (they are terminating client TLS and forwarding HTTP/1.1 to our gateway). Marking as P1 due to UX impact for tutoring sessions.
Customer - BrightTutor (2026-03-10): Repro steps and a small reproduction harness shared (link in attachments). Disabling resume reduces duplicates but not an acceptable long-term UX tradeoff.

SRE - Miguel Santos (2026-03-11): Collected serving-runtime traces for the affected session_id. Noted batch-level prefetch and an incomplete end_of_stream flag propagated from runtime to gateway when upstream request encountered a short connection reset. Suspect interplay between HTTP/2 RST_STREAM at customer edge and our streaming reconstructor. Adding ENG for deeper runtime check.

ENG - Priya Desai (2026-03-11): Theory: when a batched response is partially emitted and the batch flush aligns with a connection handoff from HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1, the server-side resume offset calculation can read the last-kv-cache boundary incorrectly resulting in replay of last tokens on resumed SSE stream and suppression of the terminal 'done' event. Will attempt a unit test to emulate HTTP/2 reset + batch flush ordering.

SRE - Miguel Santos (2026-03-12): Temporary config pushed to canary: disable 'batch-prefetch' for production-facing pools serving dedicated customers with external edge proxies. Early telemetry: duplicate-prefix rate down from ~4% to ~0.6% for the canary traffic slice. Planning rollback/gradual rollout if no regressions in cost/latency.

Support - Asha Patel (2026-03-12): Shared workaround steps and recommended edge-proxy tuning with BrightTutor (increase keepalive_timeout, avoid spurious RST_STREAM on short blips). Customer accepted canary changes and will validate production traffic next week.
